items.title: Fake histories, dubious authorship: Perumal Murugan questions Periyar Arivulagam book procurements (97)
items.summary: Controversy has erupted over book procurements at the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam library and science centre in Coimbatore after writer Perumal Murugan allegedly uncovered exorbitantly priced books of questionable authorship filled with falsified information. One such book is on a made up chief minister. Another claims that the Naladiyar—an ancient collection of Tamil poems—was a person. A third seems to attribute short stories to modern Tamil poet and writer Bharathiyaar that he likely never wrote. Perumal also raised the question if these ‘books’ are simply AI-generated text from fake publishing houses that were set up expressly for supplying to the library. The allegations have triggered a political storm between the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) and the opposition Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK), with the government announcing an inquiry into the purchases. In an article titled Periyar Arivulagathil Periya Oozhal (Major Scam in Periyar Arivulagam), published on the Tamil portal Sindhai on November 6, Perumal said he found nearly 1,800 books published by a company called Agal Vilakku Pathipagam on the library's fourth floor.
